Committee of Adjustment Meeting - Tuesday,

                        COMMITTEE OF ADJUSTMENT - CITY OF KITCHENER

                     (Pursuant to the Planning Act, R.S.O. 1990, c.P. 13, as amended,

                        and Ontario Regulations 197/96 and 200/96, as amended)

TAKE NOTICE THAT the Committee of Adjustment for the City of Kitchener will meet in Council Chambers,
2nd Floor, Kitchener City Hall, 200 King Street West, on TUESDAY, NOVEMBER 17, 2026, commencing at
10:00 a.m. for the purpose of hearing the following applications for Minor Variance and/or Consent.
Applicants or Agents must attend in support of the application. This is a public meeting. Anyone who has an
interest in any of these applications may make oral submission at the meeting or provide a written
submission for Committee consideration. Please note, this is a public meeting and will be livestreamed and
archived at www.kitchener.ca/watchnow (http://www.kitchener.ca/watchnow) .

APPLICATIONS FOR MINOR VARIANCE AND / OR CONSENT PURSUANT TO THE PLANNING ACT

A 2026-070 - 50 Victoria Street North (formerly 490-520 King Street West, 510 King Street West, 16
Victoria Street North, 50 Victoria Street North, 60 Victoria Street North)

Requesting minor variances to Zoning By-law 2019-051 to permit a surface parking space to be located 3m
from the street line rather than the minimum required 6m; to permit a front yard setback of 0m for the first
storey of the building rather than the minimum required 4.5m; to permit a landscaped area of 13% rather
than the minimum required 30%; to permit a rear yard landscaped area of 4% rather than the minimum
required 40%; to permit a Floor Space Ratio (FSR) of 0.3 rather than the minimum required 0.6; and, to
permit a building length of 115m rather than the maximum permitted 36m to facilitate the development of a
the Region of Waterloo's Transit Hub in accordance with Site Plan Application SPF26/025/K.

A 2026-071 - 75 Charles Street East

Requesting a minor variance to Zoning By-law 2019-051 to permit a parking space to be located in the front
yard and setback 1.3m from the street line rather than the minimum required 3m.

A 2026-072 - 1442 Highland Road West

Requesting minor variances to Zoning By-law 2019-051 to add a 'Restaurant' as a permitted use; and, to
permit a parking requirement of 7 parking spaces (1 space per 33 m2) rather than the minimum required 31
spaces (1 space per 7.5 m2) for the proposed 'Restaurant' use.

A 2026-073 - 23 Donnenwerth Drive

Requesting a minor variance to Zoning By-law 2019-051 to permit steps (made of a platform with
construction on piers or helical piles) in an easterly interior side yard with a setback of 0.3m rather than the
minimum required 0.75m, to facilitate the conversion of an existing Semi-Detached Dwelling to a Semi-
Detached Dwelling with an Additional Dwelling Unit (ADU)(Attached)(Semi-Detached Duplex).

A 2026-074 - 295 Guelph Street

Requesting a minor variance to Zoning By-law 2019-051 to permit a northerly exterior side yard setback of
2.6m rather than the minimum required 4.5m to recognize the use of the property for an existing triplex.

A 2026-075 - 541 Victoria Street South

Requesting a minor variance to Zoning By-law 2019-051 to permit a lot width of 27.1m rather than the
minimum required 30m to facilitate the development of the property with a 3-storey residential building
having 10 dwelling units.

B 2026-030 - 4286, 4288 & 4290 King Street East (Revised Application)

Requesting consent to sever a parcel of land municipally known as 4288 King Street East having a width of
31.3m, a depth of 125m and an area of 5,732.1sq.m. The retained land municipally known as 4286 and
4290 King Street East will have a width of 68.1m, a depth of 77m and an area of 5,352.3sq.m. Consent is
also requested to create an easement having a width of 2.4m, an irregularly shaped depth of approximately
32m and an area of 78.5sq.m. over the severed land in favour of the retained land for a water service
connection. This application is subject to minor variance applications A 2026-068 and A 2026-069; notice of
these applications were provided on October 2, 2026.

B 2026-031 - 400 Bridge Street East

Requesting consent to sever a parcel of land having a width of 105.3m, an average depth of 238.8m and an
area of 25,088sq.m. The retained land will have a width of 267.3m, an average depth of 203.5m and an
area of 50,181sq.m and is proposed to be developed with an industrial use in accordance with Site Plan
Application SP22/147/B/ES. Consent is also being requested for a partial discharge of a mortgage on the
severed land. Further, consent is being requested to create an easement for Stormwater Management
having a maximum width of 99.85m, a maximum depth of 10.02m and an area of 1078sq.m on the severed
land in favour of the retained land (shown as Part 2 on the sketch submitted with the application).

B 2026-032 - 120 Fourth Avenue

Requesting consent to sever a parcel of land having a width of 10m, a depth of 40.2m, and an area of
405.2sq.m and is proposed to be developed with a new Single Detached Dwelling with one Additional
Dwelling Unit (ADU)(Attached). The retained land will have a width of 10m, a depth of 40.2m, and an area of
405.2sq.m, and is also proposed to be developed with a new Single Detached Dwelling with one Additional
Dwelling Unit (ADU)(Attached).

B 2026-033 & A 2026-076 - 223, 229 & 235 Heiman Street

Requesting consent to permit a Partial Discharge of a Mortgage and to sever a parcel of land having a width
of 33m, a depth of 119.2m and an area of 4080.5sq.m for a future development on a lot that currently
contains two buildings having 7 dwelling units in total (a multiple dwelling). The retained land will have a

width of 31.9m, a depth of 119.2m and an area of 2597.5sq.m and will contain an existing multiple dwelling
building having 23 dwelling units. Minor variances to Zoning By-law 2019-051 are also being requested to
permit an interior side yard setback of 2.9m (between 223 and 229 Heiman Street) rather than the minimum
required 4.5m; to permit a Floor Space Ratio (FSR) of 0.09 rather than the minimum required of 0.6; and, to
permit a building height of 8m rather than the minimum required 11m, to recognize the existing buildings on
the lot proposed to be created through consent application B 2026-033.
